tierWindow.goal: Understand what generative AI is and how it works in plain terms, and recognise what it can and cannot reliably do and how to use it honestly.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Recognition, recall, description and guided application (understand and identify).
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Well-defined, one idea at a time; settled distinctions such as predicting patterns versus looking facts up, and appropriate versus inappropriate use.
tierWindow.autonomy: High scaffolding; worked examples; feedback confirms and explains; frequent low-stakes checks.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: No formal understanding of how generative AI works is assumed. The learner is early in their studies and has most likely typed a question into a chatbot such as ChatGPT without a clear sense of what the tool is, how it produces an answer, or when it can be trusted; teach from first principles.

subThemes.label: What generative AI is: a tool that produces new text or images, not a search engine or a mind
How generative AI produces output: predicting likely patterns learned from large amounts of data
Where students meet AI: chatbots, writing helpers and image or search tools in everyday study
What AI can and cannot reliably do, and why a confident answer can still be wrong
Hallucination and bias: why an AI can state something false with complete confidence
Using AI with academic integrity: honesty, acknowledgement and appropriate use

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, what generative AI is: what the tool actually does when you type a prompt. Second, what AI can and cannot do: where it is useful and why a confident answer can still be wrong. Third, using AI with integrity: how to work with these tools honestly. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about generative AI: what it is, what it can and cannot do, and how to use it honestly in your studies. By the end you will be able to explain in plain terms what a tool like a chatbot really is, describe where it is reliable and where it is not, and recognise how to use it with academic integrity.

Tools like ChatGPT are now part of student life, and knowing what they actually do matters. Understanding how they work, where they go wrong, and how to use them honestly protects your learning and your marks, whatever you are studying.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: explain what generative AI is, describe what it can and cannot do, and recognise how to use it with integrity.

practiceConnection.academic: AI tools now sit alongside your reading, writing and revision in every subject. Knowing what they are and how they fail lets you use them as a help rather than a hazard, and using them honestly keeps your work your own. The habits you build here carry into every module of your degree, and into a working life where these tools are increasingly common.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the intermediate and advanced AI and Technology courses take you into using AI on real study tasks, and then into evaluating tools, creating with them and reasoning about the wider ethics. Going wider: the same judgement underpins Criticality, Academic Writing and Referencing, where you weigh sources, write in your own voice and acknowledge your sources properly.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Generative AI is no longer a mystery box: it is a tool you can describe and use with care. You can explain what it is - something that produces likely patterns from data, rather than a mind or a search engine. You can describe what it does well and where it fails, and why a confident answer can still be wrong. And you can recognise how to use it honestly, acknowledging it where you should. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, these tools are something you use with judgement in every module. Each time you ask an AI for help, check its answer rather than trust it, and acknowledge it where your course requires, you are putting this course to work. It matters beyond your degree too: using AI honestly and knowing its limits is fast becoming an everyday working skill.
